At `(x=500, y=400)`, all three absolutely-positioned bands (`root>alpha`, `root>beta`, `root>gamma`) cover that point because each one’s bounding box includes `x=500` and `y=400`. When multiple elements overlap, the one with the highest `z-index` at that point is what’s visible. `root>beta` has `z-index: 4`, which is higher than `root>gamma` (`z-index: 3`) and `root>alpha` (`z-index: 2`), so its background color is what the viewer actually sees.

ANSWER: root>beta
